messages:
aditya: heads-up — ArgoCD in us-west-2 started returning a bunch of 429s during sync/prune waves. GPU nodepool scaleups are timing out, apps stuck in Pending. Anyone else seeing this? :eyes:

lina: yes, saw it on canary about 10m ago. argocd repo-server queue spiked and application-controller logs show repeated `Too Many Requests` from kube-apiserver.

ops-bot: [Alert] argocd-application-controller pod argocd-ctrl-2 restarted (oom/killed?) — recent spikes in reconcile queue.

charles: grabbing logs now. paste of recent tail from application-controller:```
E0907 14:12:03.123456       1 sync.go:345] error syncing application/my-team/gpu-app: apiserver response: 429 Too Many Requests
E0907 14:12:03.124001       1 sync.go:351] pruning resources: api-server rate limit exceeded
```

aditya: thanks. symptoms: big app-of-apps and appset fanout -> huge concurrent delete/create churn during a rollout. kube-apiserver is throttling, so nodepool autoscaler API calls (cloudprovider) are delayed and scaleups time out.

lina: confirming nodepool autoscaler logs show long kubernetes client backoffs — scale request never applied in time.

charles: quick mitigation idea: reduce ArgoCD concurrency for this cluster (lower operation processors + pause big appset syncs) and let autoscaler recover. Also can we pause automated rollouts in us-west temporarily?

aditya: agree. I can patch argocd-application-controller to lower concurrency to 6 and scale down repo-server parallelism. command I'll run:```
kubectl -n argocd patch deployment argocd-application-controller --type=json -p='[{"op":"replace","path":"/spec/template/spec/containers/0/args","value":["application-controller","--operation-processors=6","--status-processors=3"]}]'
```

charles: while that's rolling, set `argocd app pause` on the largest appsets in us-west (manual pause) — reduces immediate load.

lina: I'll pause the two biggest ones: `infra/gpu-pool-appset` and `prod/services-appset`.

sre-oncall: opening an incident and paging cluster infra team. tagging cloud-provider to watch nodepool API quota. Also raising apiserver request limit request to platform team for follow-up.

aditya: short-term: lower concurrency + pause appsets. mid-term: we should implement backpressure in our GitOps pipeline — detect large fanouts and auto-batch appset syncs, and add a preflight check that blocks huge concurrent deletes during scale events.

charles: +1. For long term we should also: 1) add a rate-limiter on app-of-apps controller, 2) increase kube-apiserver `--max-requests-inflight` in crisis windows (careful), 3) add a health-check that prevents garbage collection floods while autoscaler scaling.

lina: I've paused the two appsets. repo-server backlog is dropping. Nodepool autoscaler reports new nodes provisioning now.

aditya: rolling patch applied. controller concurrency reduced. observing 429s drop dramatically.

ops-bot: [Info] incident created: INC-2026-314 — GitOps backpressure causing GPU provisioning delays.

sre-oncall: action items captured in incident: (1) RCA writeup, (2) runbook for pausing appsets, (3) implement batching in appset controller, (4) alert when argocd reconcile rate > 200/min. Assigning owners.

aditya: thanks all. will post a short postmortem once we confirm recovery + follow-ups. :thumbsup:
